text.p: Swiss bonds ended lower in a relatively quiet market, with prices seen pressured by continued tightness in the short end of the market.
Swiss money rates have tended higher, reflecting what traders say are technical factors including likely borrowing by those institutions with short positions in Swiss francs.
Traders noted that Swiss bonds maintained a relatively strong tone despite a sharp drop in German federal bond prices.
The spread between Swiss and German 10-year bonds widened to 188 basis points late on Thursday YLDS3 from as narrow as levels closer to 165 last week.
Activity was dominated by several new issues.
Finland launched a 150 million Swiss franc five-year bond with a 3.25 percent coupon priced at 101.75 percent, via SBC Warburg SBHB.
Dresdner Finance set a 125 million franc, 4-1/8 percent 10-year bond priced at 102.75, via SBC amd Dresdner.

Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) followed with a 200 million Swiss franc four-year bond with a 2.5 percent coupon priced at 98.25. Deutsche Siedlungs- und Landesrentenbank (DSL) also added 100 million francs to an outstanding five-year bond launched November 6 via Credit Suisse.
One bond trader said that demand was strong for Finland and Dresdner, but UBS appeared somewhat expensive for the market.

Money rates remained fairly tight after rising sharply on Wednesday afternoon. But traders said the tightness reflected mostly technical factors tied to the franc, and some possible demand beginning to emerge at year-end.

The Swiss National Bank, as expected, left its discount rate at 1.00 percent at Thursday's weekly meeting. The rate was cut from 1.50 percent on September 26. The market was also waiting for Swiss third quarter GDP data next week. The data are expected to show a decline.
